name: GNM (Generative aNthropometric Model)
description: GNM (Generative aNthropometric Model) is Google's open ecosystem of state-of-the-art parametric statistical human models and associated perception stacks. Pronounced like 'genome' (/ˈdʒiː.noʊm/), GNM strives to be the most accurate and complete 3D parametric human model. The initial open-source release starts with GNM Head — a high-fidelity statistical 3D model of the human head with fine-grained, disentangled control over identity, expressions, and head pose, including controllable internal anatomy (eyeballs, teeth, tongue). Multi-framework support: NumPy, JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow.
keyFeatures: GNM Head: High-fidelity statistical 3D model of the human head with disentangled control over identity, expressions, and head pose
Internal Anatomy Control: Includes controllable eyeballs, teeth, and tongue for full face/head animation
Multi-Framework Support: Compatible with NumPy, JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow backends
Semantic Parameter Sampling: Supports semantically meaningful parameter sampling for human appearance generation
Open Ecosystem: Permissive Apache 2.0 license suitable for both non-commercial and commercial applications
curatorNotes: Open-source release by Google. GNM Head is the first package — a high-fidelity parametric 3D head model. Apache-2.0 license for commercial and non-commercial use. Roadmap includes full body models.
